title: Special Relativity
short_title: frames of reference, time dilation and E = mc²
standard_text: Measurement of motion depends on our frame of reference: inertial frames, the postulates of special relativity, time dilation, length contraction, and mass–energy equivalence. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 12)
meta_desc: Free Physics 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): frames of reference, time dilation and E = mc². 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The speed of light is the same in every inertial frame.
body_html:
How to think about it

Einstein's postulates: the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, and the speed of light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s) is the same for all observers. As a result, a moving clock runs slow (time dilation): t = γt₀, with γ = 1 ÷ √(1 − v²/c²).

A moving object is shorter along its motion (length contraction): L = L₀ ÷ γ. Mass and energy are equivalent: E = mc². Muons reaching the ground from the upper atmosphere are evidence for time dilation.

Example

What is γ when v = 0.6c?

1 ÷ √(1 − 0.36)

Answer: 1.25

Example

A trip lasts 10 years on Earth. Is it shorter or longer for the fast-moving traveller?

Moving clocks run slow.

Answer: shorter

Common mistakes

  • Thinking relativity only matters at everyday speeds.
  • Using the proper time in the wrong frame.
  • Thinking objects shrink in every direction.

faq.a: Its energy would have to become infinite.

What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
c: it depends on the observer's speed
items.e: It is the same in every inertial frame.

items.q: What is the Lorentz factor γ at speeds much less than the speed of light?
c: very close to 1, so relativistic effects are tiny
items.e: Relativity agrees with Newton at low speed.

items.q: In which direction does length contraction happen?
c: only along the direction of motion
at right angles to the motion only
items.e: Widths and heights are unchanged.

items.q: What is proper time?
c: the time it takes light to travel 1 m
the time between two events measured by an observer for whom they happen at the same place
the time on a clock in a moving frame seen from outside
items.e: Proper time is the shortest measured time.

items.q: Calculate the Lorentz factor γ for a speed of 0.8c.
What is an inertial frame of reference?
c: any frame on Earth's surface accelerating upwards
a frame that is not accelerating
a frame moving faster than light
items.e: Newton's first law holds in it.

items.q: Why must GPS satellites correct their clocks for relativity?
c: the speed of light changes in space
their clocks run at a different rate from clocks on the ground because of their speed and weaker gravity
items.e: Without corrections, positions would drift by kilometres a day.

items.e: Moving clocks run slow: t = γt₀ = 1.15 × 90 = 104 min.

items.q: A nuclear reaction releases 9.00 × 10<sup>13</sup> J. How much mass is converted into energy?

no evidence of an 'aether', supporting a constant speed of light
items.e: It found no change in light speed with Earth's motion.

items.q: Observers on Earth measure an astronaut's sleep on a spacecraft moving at 0.6c as 7.5 h. What is the proper time measured on board?
items.e: Proper time t₀ = t ÷ γ = 7.5 ÷ 1.25 = 6 h.

items.q: What are the two postulates of special relativity?
c: mass is always conserved and energy is not
the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, and the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers
time is absolute and space is absolute
items.e: Einstein, 1905.
